_about: PRO rewrite pass 6: era-2 scenes 40-78 in play order.

scenarios.title: The Contract Extension
scenarios.text: The club wants to talk about extending your contract a year early. The general manager calls it a sign of respect; your agent calls it a discount with a bow on it.

choices.label: Sign early for security
choices.result: Signed, a year early. Your agent says you left money on the table; you sleep fine, and the front office starts calling you 'part of the core'.

choices.label: Bet on yourself
choices.result: Declined, politely, and you play out the deal. Every kick this season is an audition for the open market, and you can feel it in your stomach.

choices.label: Talk it over at home
choices.result: The offer goes on the kitchen table for a week. You sign a shorter version that leaves room to breathe, and everyone in the house exhales.

scenarios.title: The First Big Purchase
scenarios.text: You can finally afford the car you've wanted since you were fifteen, the one on the poster above your childhood bed. The dealer already knows your name when you walk in.

choices.label: Buy it and drive it home
choices.result: Bought, and driven straight home to {parent}'s driveway. He walks around it three times without speaking, then asks for the keys.

choices.label: Buy something sensible
choices.result: Something sensible, with good mileage, and the rest goes in the bank. It's a good car. It isn't the car, and you notice every time you see one.

choices.label: Wait one more year
choices.result: A year's wait, on purpose. The wanting fades a little, and so does the fun of it, and you're not sure whether that's wisdom or a loss.

scenarios.title: The Regional Endorsement
scenarios.text: A regional grocery chain offers you a sponsorship worth more than your whole rookie salary: commercials, store openings, your face on cereal boxes in three states.

choices.label: Sign the deal
choices.result: Signed. The shoots take some weekends, the money is real, and {sibling} buys forty boxes of cereal with your face on them.

choices.label: Strike two clauses first
choices.result: The fine print, read twice, and two clauses struck: no appearances in season, no exclusivity. They agree, and you keep your Tuesdays.

choices.label: Keep your weekends
choices.result: A pass, and your weekends stay yours. A rival kicker takes the deal, and you see his face in every aisle for a year.

scenarios.title: The Investment Pitch
scenarios.text: A man at a charity dinner pitches you an investment: guaranteed returns, a famous partner, no risk. He's done this before, and he knows you can tell.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.result: You thank him and walk away. Six months later you read his name in the paper, and you pass the article to your teammates.

choices.label: Ask someone you trust
choices.result: You show it to someone you trust. They laugh, then explain exactly how it works. You learn more in an hour than in a year of statements.

choices.label: Put money in
choices.result: You put money in. The statements look great for a while, then they stop coming, and so does he. The shame lasts longer than the loss.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Mentor
scenarios.text: The club asks you to help a younger player adjust: a nervous second-year punter who eats lunch alone and calls home after every practice. Someone once did this for you.

choices.label: Take the punter on
choices.result: Meals, film, the long drives home: all of it, on your shoulders for a season. He's steadier by midseason and starts eating lunch at the specialists' table.

choices.label: Be a friend, not a mentor
choices.result: Friendly instead of formal: video games, bad movies, no lectures. He calls you when it really matters, and it does, twice.

choices.label: Point him to a veteran
choices.result: A veteran with more time and more patience gets the job, at your suggestion. It works out fine, and you feel a small pang at the specialists' table.

scenarios.title: The Locker Room Reputation
scenarios.text: Younger teammates have started looking at you when something goes wrong: a bad practice, a fight in the weight room, a rumor about a trade. You're not sure when you became that person.

choices.label: Step into it
choices.result: You step into it. When the room gets loud, you're the calm voice, and by December the coaches start running things past you first.

choices.label: Pick your moments
choices.result: Rare words, carefully chosen. You speak up twice all season, in two bad weeks, and both times the room listens completely.

choices.label: Stay a kicker
choices.result: There are captains for that, you decide, and you stay a kicker. The young players find someone else, and you're relieved and a little sorry.

scenarios.title: The Coaching Change
scenarios.text: A new special teams coach arrives with a new way of doing everything: new drills, new warmups, a new word for every old thing. He's thirty-four and very confident.

choices.label: Try every new drill
choices.result: Every new drill, without complaint, for a month. Some of it actually helps, and he notices who didn't fight him.

choices.label: Keep what works
choices.result: What works, kept; what doesn't, explained calmly. He respects the reasoning, argues once, and then adopts one of your drills.

choices.label: Get to know him first
choices.result: Lunch, his story, his family, before you judge a single drill. He turns out to be nervous, and the drills make more sense after that.

scenarios.title: The First Home Repair
scenarios.text: The roof leaks the week of a road trip, all over the living room, and the repair estimate is the size of a used car. You're in a hotel two thousand miles away.

choices.label: Handle it from the hotel
choices.result: Contractors, insurance and photos, all handled by phone from the hotel. It gets done, expensively, and you miss a meeting doing it.

choices.label: Ask {parent} to oversee it
choices.result: {parent} drives over with a ladder and an opinion, and oversees the whole repair. He loves being useful, and the roof is perfect.

choices.label: Patch it for now
choices.result: A tarp and a bucket for now, the real fix in the offseason. It's cheap, and you sleep under the sound of dripping all winter.

scenarios.title: The Charity Commitment
scenarios.text: A children's literacy nonprofit asks you to become a regular supporter: not a photo at the gala, but monthly visits, a reading program, and your name on a library wing.

choices.label: Commit to monthly visits
choices.result: Monthly visits, all year. The kids know your name by spring, and one of them reads you a whole book about a dragon who kicks.

choices.label: Bring teammates along
choices.result: Teammates, signed up one by one. It becomes a team tradition, and {holder} turns out to be the best reader of all of you.

choices.label: Write a check
choices.result: A generous check and a warm letter. It helps, and the director thanks you sincerely, and you never see the library wing.

scenarios.title: The Radio Segment
scenarios.text: A sports radio station offers you a recurring weekly segment: Monday mornings, fifteen minutes, live, with a host who likes to ask about locker-room drama.

choices.label: Take the segment
choices.result: Yes, every Monday at seven. You're good at it, the callers love you, and your Mondays disappear for the whole season into a radio booth.

choices.label: Try it for a month
choices.result: A one-month trial, then a decision. You keep it, shorter, with a promise from the host to leave the locker room alone.

choices.label: Keep your Mondays
choices.result: No segment. You'd rather talk about kicking with other kickers, and your Monday mornings stay quiet, slow and entirely yours.

scenarios.title: The Former Teammate
scenarios.text: A former teammate can't find another job in the league and keeps calling: late at night, after he's watched your games, asking if you've heard anything from anyone.

choices.label: Keep picking up
choices.result: Every call, picked up. Mostly he needs someone to listen, and some nights you stay on the phone until he's laughing again.

choices.label: Help him find other work
choices.result: Calls to people you know about jobs outside football: coaching, sales, broadcasting. One of them works out, and he sends you a photo from his new desk.

choices.label: Let some calls go
choices.result: Some calls go to voicemail. You feel bad about it every time, and you call back on Sundays, which helps a little.

scenarios.title: The New Neighborhood
scenarios.text: You've lived on this street for two years and know nobody's name. There's a block party flyer on your door and a kid next door who kicks a ball against your garage every afternoon.

choices.label: Go to the block party
choices.result: The block party, with a casserole you bought. By the end of the night you know every name on the street, and the neighbors start bringing food after losses.

choices.label: Help with the youth league
choices.result: The neighborhood youth league gets a volunteer coach once a week. The kid next door is on your team, and he's terrible, and you love it.

choices.label: Keep to yourself
choices.result: You keep to yourself. It's quiet and private, and a little lonely when the street fills with music on Saturday nights.

scenarios.title: The Financial Mistake
scenarios.text: An investment you were sure about turns out not to be smart: a restaurant that closed, a fund that froze, a statement you read three times in the car outside the facility.

choices.label: Cut the loss
choices.result: The loss, cut cleanly, and a lesson learned. It stings for a month, and then it becomes a story you tell rookies.

choices.label: Tell {love_interest} everything
choices.result: Everything, at the kitchen table, including the part you were embarrassed about. It's a hard talk and a good one, and you make the next decision together.

choices.label: Bury it in work
choices.result: Work, to forget it: early mornings, long sessions, no thinking. It doesn't quite work, and the statement is still in the glove box.

choices.label: Call the advisor you trust
choices.result: The one advisor who has always told you the truth gets a call that afternoon. You make a plan together, you stick to it, and the hole closes by spring.
choices.lock_text: having learned about money the hard way

scenarios.title: The Family Business
scenarios.text: A cousin wants your money and your name to expand the family store into three towns. The whole family is waiting for your answer, and Thanksgiving is in two weeks.

choices.label: Invest
choices.result: You invest and put your name on the sign. The opening is a family party, and for the first time in years, everyone is in one room.

choices.label: Invest, quietly
choices.result: You put in money but keep your name off the sign. It's safer, and your cousin is a little hurt by the distance.

choices.label: Turn the cousin down
choices.result: No, as kindly and clearly as you can manage. Thanksgiving is quieter this year, and you're sure it was the right answer, mostly.

scenarios.title: The Memorabilia Deal
scenarios.text: A memorabilia collector wants to pay you to sign five hundred footballs in one afternoon, in a hotel ballroom, with a man counting and a camera to prove each one is real.

choices.label: Sign all five hundred
choices.result: Five hundred signatures in one long afternoon. Your hand hurts for days, the check is large, and the man counting never smiles once.

choices.label: Add a hundred for charity
choices.result: All five hundred, plus a hundred extra for the children's hospital auction. The auction raises more than your check, and the collector pays for the extra hundred.

choices.label: Sign for kids at the fence
choices.result: No ballroom, no counting man. You'd rather sign for kids at the practice fence, for free, and you do, every Thursday.

scenarios.title: The Young Kicker's Question
scenarios.text: A college kicker emails you for career advice. It's a long email, carefully written, and the question at the end is a good one: how do you know when to change and when to wait?

choices.label: Write a real answer
choices.result: A long, honest answer, written over two evenings. He prints it out, and two years later he sends you a photo of it taped inside his locker.

choices.label: Call him instead
choices.result: A phone call instead of an email. You talk for an hour, and he sounds exactly like you did at twenty, which is strange and a little moving.

choices.label: Send a short reply
choices.result: A short, kind reply and a 'good luck'. He's grateful, and you wonder later what the longer answer would have been.

scenarios.title: The Retirement Savings
scenarios.text: A financial advisor reviews your long-term plan and asks a question you can't answer: what does your life cost after football, per year, in today's money?

choices.label: Learn the answer
choices.result: The answer, learned over two weeks of spreadsheets, and the next ten questions too. You understand your own money for the first time, and it's calming.

choices.label: Bring {parent} to the next meeting
choices.result: {parent} comes to the next meeting with a legal pad and better questions than yours. You make the plan together, and he insists on paying for lunch.

choices.label: Trust the advisor
choices.result: The advisor knows best, you decide, and stop asking questions. It's easy and restful, and you never learn the number.

scenarios.title: The Public Appearance
scenarios.text: You're invited to a high-profile charity gala in black tie: actors, owners, a senator, a string quartet. You don't own a tuxedo, and the event is Saturday.

choices.label: Go and enjoy it
choices.result: A rented tuxedo, a long night and people you didn't know existed. You enjoy it more than you expected, and someone from a children's charity asks for your number.

choices.label: Go with a purpose
choices.result: A plan, three introductions, and home by eleven. You leave with three useful numbers and a sponsor for your youth camp.

choices.label: Stay home
choices.result: Home, in sweatpants, with takeout and a movie. Nobody at the gala notices except your agent, who sends a single sad emoji at midnight.

scenarios.title: The Family Holiday
scenarios.text: The schedule lands on a family holiday again, the third year in a row. {parent} has already set a place for you at the table, just in case.

choices.label: Bring the holiday to you
choices.result: The whole family, flown in for the weekend. Dinner is in a hotel ballroom, and it's still home, and {sibling} carves the turkey badly.

choices.label: Keep your routine and call
choices.result: Your routine, and a long call between meetings. They put you on speaker at the table, and you hear everyone laughing.

choices.label: Plan a second celebration
choices.result: A second holiday, planned for the bye week, with everything: the dishes, the games, the arguments. Everyone says it's fine. It mostly is.

scenarios.title: The Teammates' Dispute
scenarios.text: Two teammates ask you to settle an argument about who gets the corner locker by the heater. It's been going on for a week, and they both say you're the only fair one.

choices.label: Make them talk it out
choices.result: Both of them, in a room, talking it out in front of you. It takes forty minutes, ends with a handshake, and they decide to share.

choices.label: Pick the right side
choices.result: The right side, after listening to both. One of them sulks for a week, and then admits you were right, grudgingly.

choices.label: Let them settle it
choices.result: Settle it yourselves, you tell them, and walk away. They do, eventually, with a coin flip, some shouting and a handshake.

scenarios.title: The Injury Prevention Program
scenarios.text: The club wants you on a new training and recovery program: sleep tracking, cold tubs, a mobility routine at six in the morning. The sports science staff is very excited about it.

choices.label: Follow it to the letter
choices.result: Every piece of it, exactly. Your legs feel younger by October, and the sports science staff starts using your numbers in presentations.

choices.label: Add your own work
choices.result: The program, plus your own work on top. You're stronger and more tired, and the staff worries quietly about the extra load.

choices.label: Do the minimum
choices.result: The minimum: the cold tubs, never the six o'clock mobility. The trainers notice right away, and so, by December, does your hip.

scenarios.title: The Younger Teammate's Mistake
scenarios.text: A rookie makes a mistake: he missed a meeting, then lied about why. He comes to you, not the coaches, white-faced, asking what to do before anyone finds out.

choices.label: Walk him to the coaches
choices.result: Down the hall, together, and you stand beside him while he tells them. It goes better than he feared, and he never lies to a coach again.

choices.label: Listen first
choices.result: Listening first, all of it, and then helping him find the words. He goes in alone, which matters to him.

choices.label: Tell him what you'd do
choices.result: Exactly what you'd do, step by step. He does it, it works, and he thanks you without quite looking at you.

scenarios.title: The Personal Trainer
scenarios.text: A private trainer who works with three Olympic athletes could change your whole offseason, for a price that makes your advisor wince. They have one opening.

choices.label: Hire the trainer
choices.result: Hired, for the summer. It's brutal and scientific, and you come back to camp faster, leaner and slightly afraid of the trainer.

choices.label: Ask for a trial week
choices.result: A trial week first. It's good, so you hire them for half the summer, and keep the other half for your own work.

choices.label: Train the way you always have
choices.result: Your own routine, the one that got you here. It's familiar and cheaper, and you wonder all summer what you're missing.

scenarios.title: Dinner With Influential People
scenarios.text: Your agent invites you to a private dinner with influential people in the league: two owners, a network executive and a former commissioner. Dress code: 'nice'.

choices.label: Be yourself
choices.result: Good stories, honestly told, and you laugh at your own mistakes. Two of the owners remember your name the next season.

choices.label: Mostly listen
choices.result: Mostly listening. You learn how the league actually works, who decides what and why, and you write it all down in the car.

choices.label: Skip the dinner
choices.result: No dinner. Your agent sighs and goes alone, and comes back with a story about you that isn't quite true.

scenarios.title: The Team's Future
scenarios.text: The franchise is talking about a full rebuild: younger, cheaper, faster. A reporter says there's a list of veterans who might be traded, and your name is on it.

choices.label: Make yourself essential
choices.result: The one veteran they can't rebuild without: that's the plan, and you work like it. The list changes by spring.

choices.label: Have your agent find out
choices.result: Your agent finds out which list it is. It's the good one, for now, and you breathe for the first time in a week.

choices.label: Invest in the young players
choices.result: The young players get your time, because they're the future and so, maybe, are you. The coaches notice who's helping.

scenarios.title: The New Family Responsibility
scenarios.text: A family member needs more of your time than the season has: {sibling} is going through a divorce, and calls every night after the kids are asleep.

choices.label: Make the time
choices.result: Flights on off days, calls every night. You're exhausted and present, and {sibling} says later that you were the reason they got through it.

choices.label: Build a plan with the family
choices.result: A family plan, so nobody carries it alone: {parent} takes Mondays, you take Thursdays, everyone takes Sunday. It works better than anyone hoped.

choices.label: Promise the offseason
choices.result: The offseason, promised, and kept. It's a long wait for both of you, and the calls in between are short.

scenarios.title: The Fourth Season
scenarios.text: Your fourth pro season. Nobody calls you a rookie anymore, the equipment manager knows your cleat size by heart, and two of this year's rookies ask for your autograph.

choices.label: Look out for the rookies
choices.result: The rookies get looked after, the way someone once looked after you: rides, meals, the names of the people who matter.

choices.label: Raise your own bar
choices.result: Nobody else will raise your bar now, so you do it yourself: new goals, written down and taped to the bathroom mirror.

choices.label: Enjoy the ease
choices.result: Some ease, finally earned. You enjoy this season more than any before it, and the snapper says you look five years younger.

scenarios.title: The Comfortable Routine
scenarios.text: Your routine works so well it's starting to feel like a rut. Same breakfast, same warmup, same thoughts at the same moments. You haven't felt nervous in a month, and you miss it.

choices.label: Change one small thing
choices.result: One small change: a different song in your warmup. It's enough to wake you up, and your first kick that day feels new.

choices.label: Push harder inside it
choices.result: Harder, inside the exact same routine. It's tiring, and it works, and slowly the rut starts to feel like a groove again.

choices.label: Trust the rut
choices.result: A rut that works is a groove, you decide, and you trust it. The season goes on quietly and well.

scenarios.title: The Raise
scenarios.text: Your second contract is real money, and everyone you know has noticed: old friends with ideas, cousins with emergencies, a teacher from middle school with a fundraiser.

choices.label: Set one rule for everyone
choices.result: One rule, for everyone, written down. It's fair, it's a little lonely, and the calls slow down within a month.

choices.label: Help the ones who need it
choices.result: The people who really need it get help, quietly, and nobody else hears about it. {parent} finds out anyway and is proud.

choices.label: Change your number
choices.result: A new phone number, given to twelve people. Things get quieter immediately, and two old friends feel shut out and say so.

scenarios.title: The House With a Yard
scenarios.text: You buy a house with a backyard big enough for a kicking net. The previous owners left a swing set, a lemon tree and a note wishing you luck.

choices.label: Put up the net
choices.result: The net goes up the first weekend. The neighbors watch from their windows, and by Sunday their kids are shagging balls for you.

choices.label: Throw a housewarming
choices.result: Everyone, over, the first Saturday: family, teammates, neighbors. {parent} gives the tour twice, and {sibling} falls off the swing set.

choices.label: Sit under the lemon tree
choices.result: Nothing, in the backyard, under the lemon tree, for a whole afternoon. It's the first time in years you've done nothing on purpose.

scenarios.title: The Specialist Who Retires
scenarios.text: The punter you've worked beside for six years retires suddenly, with a two-line statement on a Tuesday afternoon. He hasn't returned anyone's calls since, including yours.

choices.label: Throw him a send-off
choices.result: A send-off with the specialists at his favorite diner, whether he likes it or not. He comes, finally, and it's loud and long.

choices.label: Help the new punter settle
choices.result: The new punter gets your time and the old punter's tricks, passed along. The unit stays steady through the change.

choices.label: Give him his quiet
choices.result: His quiet, respected. You send one short message and wait, and a month later he calls you first, from a lake.

scenarios.title: A Different Snap
scenarios.text: A new long snapper arrives, and for the first time in years your timing is off. The ball comes faster, flatter, with a spin you don't recognize, and the misses are in practice for everyone to see.

choices.label: Rep it out after practice
choices.result: After every practice, an extra fifty snaps until the timing is back. Your leg is heavy and your rhythm returns by week three.

choices.label: Get to know him first
choices.result: Off the field first: dinners, his family, his terrible music. The timing follows the trust, the way it always does, within two weeks.

choices.label: Film every snap
choices.result: Every snap, filmed and studied. You find the tenth of a second in the film room, and fix it in one afternoon.

scenarios.title: The Podcast Guest Spot
scenarios.text: A popular podcast wants you as a weekly guest. The host likes controversy and has a reputation for getting athletes to say things about their teammates.

choices.label: Set your terms first
choices.result: Terms, agreed up front: no teammates, no coaches, no locker room. It's good radio anyway, and the host respects the line.

choices.label: Say yes and wing it
choices.result: Yes, and you're great at it, until the fourth episode, when you say too much about a teammate. You apologize to him in person.

choices.label: Pass on the podcast
choices.result: No podcast this year. The host finds another kicker, who says something he regrets by October, and you're quietly relieved.

scenarios.title: The Teammate Who Becomes a Friend
scenarios.text: A teammate has become your closest friend in the league: same humor, same bad taste in movies, families who get along. You realize it on a road trip, laughing at three in the morning.

choices.label: Make time for it
choices.result: Time, made on purpose: dinners, families, the off days together. The friendship becomes the best part of the whole job.

choices.label: Train together all summer
choices.result: A whole summer of training together, every morning. You both get better, and the friendship gets a rhythm of its own.

choices.label: Keep it easy
choices.result: No effort required, and none spent. Some friendships don't need any work at all, and this one never does, even years later.

scenarios.title: The Holder's Wedding
scenarios.text: {holder} asks you to be in the wedding party. It's in June, in {holder}'s hometown, and there's a rehearsal dinner where you're expected to say something.

choices.label: Say yes and give a toast
choices.result: Yes, and a toast at the rehearsal dinner that nobody forgets: the first hold, the bad haircut, the night they saved your season.

choices.label: Organize the weekend
choices.result: The whole weekend, organized by you: the hotel block, the shuttle, the backup suits. {holder} doesn't lift a finger and cries about it.

choices.label: Show up and enjoy it
choices.result: Showing up, standing where they tell you, dancing badly at the reception. You enjoy every minute, and {holder} says it was perfect.

scenarios.title: The Fan Club
scenarios.text: Fans start an official fan club in your name, with T-shirts and a newsletter. They want you at the first meeting, in the back room of a pizza place on a Tuesday.

choices.label: Go to the meeting
choices.result: Two hours in the back room of the pizza place. They make you an honorary member, and the T-shirt becomes your favorite shirt.

choices.label: Send a message and a ball
choices.result: A recorded message and a signed ball for the raffle. They play the message three times and frame the ball.

choices.label: Thank them online
choices.result: A thank-you post, and your Tuesday stays your own. The club grows anyway, without you, which feels a little strange and kind of nice.

scenarios.title: The Rival's Big Contract
scenarios.text: {tyler} signs a bigger contract than yours, by a lot, and the media want a comment. A reporter reads you the number, slowly, and waits.

choices.label: Congratulate him
choices.result: Congratulations, publicly, and you mean it. He texts you thanks within the hour and a photo of the two of you at seventeen.

choices.label: Decline to comment
choices.result: No comment, politely, and you walk away from the cameras. It makes a headline anyway: 'Kicker silent on rival's huge new deal.'

choices.label: Keep the number private
choices.result: The number, written on a card, goes inside your locker where only you can see it. Every practice that month has a little more in it.

scenarios.title: The Charity Golf Tournament
scenarios.text: You host your own charity golf tournament for the first time: thirty-six foursomes, a silent auction, and a sponsor who keeps asking for 'more visibility'.

choices.label: Run it yourself
choices.result: Every detail, run by you, from the sign-up sheet to the last trophy. You're exhausted, and the tournament raises twice the goal.

choices.label: Invite the old college crew
choices.result: Your college teammates, invited, and {best_friend} runs the auction. It turns into a reunion, and the bidding gets very competitive.

choices.label: Find a sponsor to run it
choices.result: A sponsor who covers everything and handles the details. It raises more than you'd have alone, and feels less like yours.

scenarios.title: The Investment Club
scenarios.text: A group of teammates forms an investment club: monthly meetings, a shared account, a lot of opinions about technology stocks. They want you in, and the first meeting is at the quarterback's house.

choices.label: Join the club
choices.result: Joined. The meetings are mostly jokes and some good ideas, and the account does fine, and the friendships do better.

choices.label: Join with limits
choices.result: In, with a small amount and one rule: nothing you don't understand. You end up explaining index funds to a linebacker, who becomes your biggest convert.

choices.label: Keep money and friends apart
choices.result: Money and friends don't mix, for you. You stay out, politely, and still go to the meetings for the food.
